🎯 Ming "Tommy" Tang posted: Three things people call bugs in LLMs. They are features. If you use AI tools for real work and you do not understand this, you will get burned. LLMs are probabilistic. Same prompt, slightly different answer. If you need 100 percent reproducibility, use a different tool. If your workflow leans on a commercial model and Anthropic ships a new version tomorrow, your outputs shift with it. Not a defect. The design. They hallucinate. Even the frontier models. At an airport last week I asked Claude where to buy a gift. It named a store. I walked over. The store did not exist. I went back and pushed the model. It agreed the store did not exist. Opus 4.8. frontier model. Still wrong. For a gift, annoying. For a variant call or a drug target, dangerous. You have to judge the output. If you cannot tell whether the answer is right, do not use an agent for the task. Use a deterministic tool and read the output yourself. Think about what your AI tool actually depends on. Continuity: if the provider pulls the model or changes weights, your workflow moves. For stable work, run open-weights models locally. Reproducibility: not solved. Hallucination: not going away. Design around all three. An AI tool is better than most people. It is not better than an expert with twenty years in the field. If you are the expert, the AI is a force multiplier. If you are not, it is a plausible-sounding coin flip you have no way to check. Stop treating probabilism, hallucination, and model drift like bugs Anthropic will fix next quarter. They will not. Build your work around what LLMs actually are. That is the whole game. I hope you've found this post helpful. Follow me for more.
